own_solution.law: Lagrangian / rotating-frame dynamics of a bead on a hoop spinning about its vertical diameter: R theta'' = -g sin(theta) + omega^2 R sin(theta) cos(theta); off-axis equilibrium cos(theta0) = g/(omega^2 R); small-oscillation angular frequency Omega = omega sin(theta0)
assumptions: frictionless bead, hoop rotating at constant omega
omega^2 R > g so the off-axis equilibrium exists (19.6 > 9.8 m/s^2)

defect_reasons.other: T4B28 says the platform 'was set rising with a constant upward acceleration ... before the oscillations were observed' without saying explicitly that the acceleration continues during the oscillations; the natural reading (still accelerating) gives R, but a reader could take it as a past phase.

notes: Base: omega^2 R = 49*0.4 = 19.6 m/s^2, cos(theta0) = 9.8/19.6 = 0.5, theta0 = 60 deg; Omega = 7 sin60 = 6.0622 rad/s; T = 2 pi/Omega = 1.0365 s. With platform upward acceleration 2.1 m/s^2 during oscillation, g_eff = 11.9: cos(theta0) = 0.60714, sin^2 = 0.63138, Omega^2 = 30.938, Omega = 5.5622 rad/s, T = 1.1296 s (still in the off-axis regime since 11.9 < 19.6). Bead mass cancels from the equation of motion (C). Crane hook and earlier-run sentences are D. All numbered acceleration sentences state 2.1 m/s^2; mass sentences both 26 g; 'a few metres per second squared' sentences are number-free.
